questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct statement(s) regarding sugars is(are)
Given: Specific rotations of L-($-$)-glucose and L-($+$)-fructose are $-52.5^\circ$ and $+92.5^\circ$, respectively.
options: On treatment with $\text{HNO}_3$, gluconic acid is oxidized to saccharic acid, whereas glucose is not oxidized to saccharic acid.
Fructose gives a positive Fehling's test because it isomerises to glucose and another aldohexose in the presence of Fehling's reagent.
Invert sugar is an equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose formed after hydrolysis of the corresponding disaccharide.
Specific rotation of invert sugar is $-40^\circ$.
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect: Nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$) is a strong oxidizing agent that oxidizes both glucose and gluconic acid to saccharic acid.

Statement (B) is correct: Fehling's reagent provides an alkaline medium. Under these conditions, fructose (a ketose) undergoes the Lobry de Bruyn-van Ekenstein rearrangement to form an equilibrium mixture of fructose, glucose, and mannose. Glucose and mannose are aldohexoses that readily reduce Fehling's solution, giving a positive test.

Statement (C) is correct: Hydrolysis of sucrose (a disaccharide) yields an equimolar mixture of D-($+$)-glucose and D-($-$)-fructose. This mixture is known as invert sugar because the sign of specific rotation changes from positive (for sucrose) to negative (for the mixture).

Statement (D) is incorrect: The specific rotation of L-($-$)-glucose is $-52.5^\circ$, so for D-($+$)-glucose it is $+52.5^\circ$. The specific rotation of L-($+$)-fructose is $+92.5^\circ$, so for D-($-$)-fructose it is $-92.5^\circ$.
The specific rotation of invert sugar (an equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose, which have the same molar mass) is the average of their specific rotations:
$[\alpha]_{\text{mix}} = \dfrac{+52.5^\circ + (-92.5^\circ)}{2} = -20^\circ$.

Answer: Fructose gives a positive Fehling's test because it isomerises to glucose and another aldohexose in the presence of Fehling's reagent.; Invert sugar is an equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose formed after hydrolysis of the corresponding disaccharide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the following reaction sequence, major products $\textbf{X}$ and $\textbf{Y}$ are acyclic monomers.

$500$ mol of $\textbf{X}$ completely reacts with $500$ mol of $\textbf{Y}$ to give $1$ mol of a single biodegradable acyclic copolymer $\textbf{Z}$ as the only product. The amount of $\textbf{Z}$ formed in grams is ____.
Given:
Atomic mass (in amu): H : $1$, C : $12$, N : $14$, O : $16$, Br : $80$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identification of monomer $\textbf{X}$
The given reaction sequence for $\textbf{X}$ is:
$\text{CH}_3\text{I} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{CH}_3\text{CN}$
$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$
$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{Red P, Br}_2} \text{BrCH}_2\text{COOH}$ (Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction)
$\text{BrCH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3 \text{ (excess)}} \text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$
Thus, $\textbf{X}$ is Glycine.
Molar mass of $\textbf{X}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2$) = $2(12) + 5(1) + 14 + 2(16) = 75 \text{ g/mol}$.

Step 2: Identification of monomer $\textbf{Y}$
Caprolactam on acidic hydrolysis gives $\epsilon$-aminocaproic acid:
Caprolactam $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \text{H}_2\text{N}-(\text{CH}_2)_5-\text{COOH}$
Thus, $\textbf{Y}$ is $\epsilon$-aminocaproic acid.
Molar mass of $\textbf{Y}$ ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{13}\text{NO}_2$) = $6(12) + 13(1) + 14 + 2(16) = 131 \text{ g/mol}$.

Step 3: Calculation of the mass of copolymer $\textbf{Z}$
The copolymer $\textbf{Z}$ is Nylon-2-nylon-6, which is a biodegradable polyamide formed by the condensation polymerization of Glycine and $\epsilon$-aminocaproic acid.
The problem states that $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{X}$ and $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{Y}$ completely react to form $1 \text{ mol}$ of a single acyclic copolymer $\textbf{Z}$.
This means each molecule of polymer $\textbf{Z}$ contains $500$ units of $\textbf{X}$ and $500$ units of $\textbf{Y}$, making a total of $1000$ monomer units.
In an acyclic chain of $1000$ monomers, the number of peptide (amide) bonds formed is $1000 - 1 = 999$.
For each peptide bond formed, one molecule of water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is eliminated. Since $1 \text{ mol}$ of polymer $\textbf{Z}$ is formed, $999 \text{ mol}$ of water are eliminated.

Applying the law of conservation of mass:
Mass of $\textbf{Z}$ = (Mass of $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{X}$) + (Mass of $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{Y}$) - (Mass of $999 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$)
Mass of $\textbf{Z} = (500 \times 75) + (500 \times 131) - (999 \times 18)$
Mass of $\textbf{Z} = 37500 + 65500 - 17982$
Mass of $\textbf{Z} = 103000 - 17982 = 85018 \text{ g}$

Answer: $85018$

A linear octasaccharide (molar mass $=1024 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ) on complete hydrolysis produces three monosaccharides: ribose, 2-deoxyribose and glucose. The amount of 2-deoxyribose formed is $58.26 \%(\mathrm{w} / \mathrm{w})$ of the total amount of the monosaccharides produced in the hydrolyzed products. The number of ribose unit(s) present in one molecule of octasaccharide is $\qquad$
Use : Molar mass $\left(\right.$ in $\left.\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}\right)$ : ribose $=150,2$-deoxyribose $=134$, glucose $=180$; Atomic mass (in amu): $\mathrm{H}=1, \mathrm{O}=16$
questions.solution:
$\underset{\mathrm{M} . \mathrm{M} .=1024}{\text{ Octasaccharide }}+\underset{\mathrm{M} . \mathrm{M} .=126}{7 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}} \longrightarrow \begin{aligned} & \text{ Ribose }+ \text{ 2deoxyribose }+ \text{ glucose } \\ & \text{ Total mass }=1024+126=1150\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}
& 58.26=\frac{134 \times n}{1150} \times 100 \\
& \frac{66.999}{100}=134 n \quad n=4.99=5
\end{aligned}$5 units of 2-Deoxyribose
$1150=(5 \times 150)+(\mathrm{x} \times 150)+(\mathrm{y} \times 180) \begin{aligned} & 1150=\underbrace{750}_{5 \text{ unit }}+\underbrace{150 x}_{300}+\underbrace{180 y}_{180} \\ 
& \qquad \quad \qquad \quad \text{2 unit} \quad  \text{1 unit}\end{aligned}$
n = 2.00

questions.q: For a double strand DNA, one strand is given below: The amount of energy required to split the double strand DNA into two single strands is _______ kcal $\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. [Given: Average energy per $\mathrm{H}$-bond for A-T base pair $=1.0 \mathrm{kcal} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{G}-\mathrm{C}$ base pair $=1.5 \mathrm{kcal}$ $\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, and A-U base pair $=1.25 \mathrm{kcal} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. Ignore electrostatic repulsion between the phosphate groups.]
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{T} \quad 2 \mathrm{H}$-bond
$\mathrm{G} \equiv \mathrm{C} \quad 3 \mathrm{H}$-bond
Number of $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{T}$ pair $=7$
Number of $\mathrm{G} \equiv \mathrm{C}$ pair $=6$
Number of H-bond involve in $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{T}=7 \times 2=14$
Number of $\mathrm{H}$-bond involve in $\mathrm{G} \equiv \mathrm{C}=6 \times 3=18$
Energy required for $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{T}=14 \times 1=14$
Energy required for $\mathrm{G} \equiv \mathrm{C}=18 \times 1.5=27$
Total energy required $14+27=41$

questions.q: A tetrapeptide has -COOH group on alanine. This produces glycine (Gly), Valine (Val), Phenyl alanine (Phe) and Alanine (Ala) on complete hydrolysis. For this tetrapeptide, the number of possible sequences (primary structures) with -NH<sub>2</sub> group attached to a chiral center is
questions.solution:
Following combinations are possible for tetrapeptide:
$\begin{array}{ll}\text{Val} - \text{Phe} - \text{Gly} - \text{Ala} \\ \text{Val} - \text{Gly} - \text{Phe} - \text{Ala} \\ \text{Phe} - \text{Gly} - \text{Val} - \text{Gly} \\ \text{Phe} - \text{Val} - \text{Gly} - \text{Ala}\end{array}$
In all above sequences, C-terminal is alanine.
Glycine is optically inactive amino acid, it can not be N-terminal. Hence, only above combinations are possible.

When the following aldohexose exists in its D-configuration, the total number of stereoisomers in its pyranose form is :

questions.q:
The substituents $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ for nine peptides are listed in the table given below. How many of these peptides are positively charged at $\mathrm{pH}=7.0$ ?



$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}

\hline Peptide & \mathbf{R}_{\mathbf{1}} & \mathbf{R}_{\mathbf{2}} \\

\hline I & \mathrm{H}& \mathrm{H}\\

\hline II & \mathrm{H}& \mathrm{CH}_{3}\\

\hline III & \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{COOH}& \mathrm{H}\\

\hline IV & \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CONH}_{2}& \left(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\right)_{4} \mathrm{NH}_{2}\\

\hline V & \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CONH}_{2}& \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CONH}_{2}\\

\hline VI & \left(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\right)_{4} \mathrm{NH}_{2}& \left(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\right)_{4} \mathrm{NH}_{2}\\

\hline VII & \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{COOH}& \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CONH}_{2}\\

\hline VIII & \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{OH}& \left(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\right)_{4} \mathrm{NH}_{2}\\

\hline IX & \left(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\right)_{4} \mathrm{NH}_{2}& \mathrm{CH}_{3}\\

\hline

\end{array}$
questions.solution: Peptides with isoelectric point (pI) more than 7 would exist as cation in neutral solution $(\mathrm{pH}=7)$ which means the given polypeptide is of basic nature, so it must contain two or more amino groups. Hence IV, VI, VIII and IX are correct options.

questions.q: A decapeptide (molecular weight 796) on complete hydrolysis gives glycine (molecular weight 75), alanine and phenylalanine. Glycine contributes $47.0 \%$ to the total weight of the hydrolysed products. The number of glycine units present in the decapeptide is
questions.solution: $\text{ A decapeptide has nine peptide (amide) linkage as }$ \\ Therefore, no hydrolysis, it will absorb nine water molecules. Hence, total mass of hydrolysis product $=796+18 \times 9=958\Rightarrow$ mass of glycine in hydrolysis product $=\frac{958 \times 47}{100}=450\Rightarrow$ number of glycine molecule in one molecule of decapeptide $=\frac{450}{75}=6$

Statement II Reaction of glucose with Fehling's solution gives $\mathrm{CuO}$ and gluconic acid.
options:
Statement I is true, Statement II is true, Statement II is a correct explanation for Statement I
